name: Northern Pacific trestle over the Little Missouri
location_evidence: Train "rumbled across three hundred feet of trestle" before stopping at Little Missouri (HAG ch. I). Ford was "a hundred yards north of the trestle" (HAG ch. I). People walked the trestle to cross at high water (HAG).
sources: HAG ch. I; HAG (spring flood passage)
notes: Anchor feature. Current rail line likely follows the same alignment; confirm against GLO plat and NP right-of-way maps.

name: Little Missouri station (first depot)
location_evidence: "The 'town' of Little Missouri consisted of a group of primitive buildings scattered about the shack which did duty as a railroad station" with no platform (HAG ch. I). A "new depot will be soon completed" (Dickinson Press, quoted in HAG).
sources: HAG ch. I; Prairie Public Dakota Datebook 2025-09-18 (depot moved to Medora)
notes: Two depots may be involved (the shack, then the "new depot"). Need NP station records.

name: Pyramid Park Hotel
location_evidence: "stood immediately north of the tracks" (HAG ch. I). T.R. walked to "a huge black building looming northeastward" from the depot (HAG ch. I).
sources: HAG ch. I (loft with 14 beds, T.R.'s first night, Sept. 7-8, 1883); AUTO ch. IV [P]; TRC Cantonment entry
notes: Managed by Capt. Vine, Frank Vine's father (HAG ch. II). TRC places it on the west bank. Highest-priority photo search.

name: Bill Williams's saloon (Little Missouri)
location_evidence: "beside it [the hotel] stood the one-story palace of sin" (HAG ch. I).

name: Johnny Nelson's store
location_evidence: "South of the track ... Johnny Nelson kept a store" (HAG ch. I).

name: Mrs. McGeeney's boarding house
location_evidence: "in Mrs. McGeeney's boarding-house next door" to Nelson's store; within fifty feet of Mrs. Fitzgerald (HAG ch. I, III).
notes: P. McGeeney "will have a fine hotel when it is completed" (Dickinson Press in HAG). Possibly a second, later building.

name: Section foreman Fitzgerald's shack
location_evidence: "Directly to the east, on the brink of the river" (HAG ch. I). Within 50 ft of McGeeney's, so probably south of the track (inferred).

name: Jake Maunders's shack
location_evidence: "At a corresponding place on the other side of the track" from Fitzgerald (HAG ch. I), so probably north of the track (inferred).

name: The Cantonment (abandoned army post)
removed: part burned early 1887; rest razed or hauled off; hospital moved to Dickinson fall 1888
use: army post then ranch HQ and hotel
location_evidence: "A quarter of a mile west of" Maunders's shack, "in a grove of cottonwood trees" (HAG ch. I). Eleven buildings around a parade ground (TRC).
photos: none found yet (TRC Cantonment page uses an SHSND photo of Medora)
sources: TRC encyclopedia "Cantonment"; HAG ch. I-II; Prairie Public 2025-09-18
notes: Buildings: barracks, 4 officers' quarters, 9-bed hospital, storehouse, blacksmith, 2 laundress quarters, admin, bakery, guardhouse, ice house, stables for 22 animals (TRC). Army left March 24, 1883; bought by H. H. Gorringe's group (May 1883 per HAG; $1,500 per TRC). Army construction records (National Archives, Quartermaster) may have plans.

name: Jerry Paddock's livery stable
location_evidence: No location given (HAG ch. III).

name: Huts, miners' shacks, two frame houses under construction
location_evidence: "A few huts in the sagebrush, a half-dozen miners' shacks under the butte to the south, and one or two rather pretentious frame houses in process of construction" (HAG ch. I).
notes: Also Anderson's restaurant and J. B. Walker's business, named in Dickinson Press notes quoted by HAG ch. IV.

name: Railroad shipping corrals
location_evidence: "the shipping corrals near the Cantonment" (HAG).

name: Chateau de Mores
location_evidence: About half a mile southwest of Medora on the west bank, on the bench above the river (NRHP; Hagedorn photo from the east bank).
sources: NRHP 75001299; SHSND Chateau history; NRHP 77001018 (Von Hoffman House)
notes: Still standing, so it can be measured or modeled from existing drawings. Ask SHSND about a Historic Structure Report and outbuildings (stable, servants' quarters).

name: De Mores company office and store
location_evidence: In the 1919 panorama labels (HAG plate p. 402). Exact lot TBD.
photos: trc:3013533 ("Medora in 1883"); HAG plate p. 48 (winter 1883-84); HAG plate p. 402 (1919)
notes: Good candidate for a photo-based massing model.

name: First abattoir
location_evidence: Same complex as the 1885 plant (inferred).
sources: HAG (25 head a day; replaced because inefficient)
notes: NRHP says the plant "completed and began operating in 1883" and does not mention two phases. Reconcile with SHSND.

name: De Mores abattoir (packing plant)
footprint_ft: abattoir 105 x 180; power house 30 x 40; cooper shop 25 x 30; fertilizer room 30 x 38; three ice houses 40 x 100 each
location_evidence: NE1/4 NE1/4 Sec. 27, T140N R102W, on the east bank at the west edge of Medora. NRHP boundary approx. 46.9156-46.9183 N, 103.5247-103.5311 W. Surviving chimney and foundations mark the corners (WPA markers).
notes: Capacity varies by source: 100 head/day (HAG, 1885), 150 (NRHP), 200 (NPS Historical Handbook). Note it.

name: The Marquis's ice dam
location_evidence: "the Marquis built a dam nearby for the purpose of securing ice" near the trestle (HAG).

name: Metropolitan Hotel
location_evidence: Current Rough Riders Hotel site (verify original footprint vs. 1960s restoration and 2010 expansion).
sources: SAH Archipedia ND-01-BI1; HAG plate caption
notes: Built by George Fitzgerald (SAH). Was this the same Fitzgerald as the section foreman? Unknown.

name: Hotel de Mores
location_evidence: TBD
photos: trc:3013534; trc:3013529 (interior group); trc:3013559 (1895, jury effigy in front); HAG plate p. 332
sources: HAG quoting Mandan Pioneer ("a large hotel" among the new brick buildings)
notes: Fate and site unknown. High-priority question for SHSND.

name: St. Mary's Catholic Church
location_evidence: Fourth Street and Third Avenue (NRHP).
notes: Built by Peter Book. Belfry and rear chimney are later or altered; check the 1941 changes before modeling.

name: Von Hoffman House
location_evidence: Lots 7-10, Block 15, Original Plat of Medora; Broadway and Fifth Street (NRHP).
notes: Built by Peter Book for the Marquise's parents.

name: Joe Ferris's store (Medora)
location_evidence: "on the eastern bank" (HAG). Next to Fisher's roller rink and opposite the Bad Lands Cow Boy office (HAG ch. on Medora).
notes: T.R. kept a room upstairs on visits (HAG; TRC).

name: Bad Lands Cow Boy office
location_evidence: "opposite the office of the Bad Lands Cowboy" from Joe Ferris's store (HAG).
photos: trc:3013536 (Packard and wife at the door)
notes: The Library of Congress catalogs the early 1884 issues as published at Little Missouri, so there may have been an earlier office on the west bank.

name: Fisher's roller-skating pavilion
location_evidence: "next to Joe's store, opposite the office of the Bad Lands Cowboy" (HAG).

name: Bill Williams's saloon and hall (Medora)
location_evidence: First a small building "near Joe's store," which burned; then a two-story frame building the Marquis built for him (HAG).
notes: The upstairs hall held meetings, dances and church services. Possibly the "town hall" where T.R. greeted people in 1903; unconfirmed.

name: Northern Pacific depot (Medora)
location_evidence: Labeled in the 1919 panorama (HAG plate p. 402).
notes: Services were held in its baggage room (HAG).

name: Black Hills freight depot
use: freight depot for the stage and forwarding company
location_evidence: No location given.
sources: Mandan Pioneer, quoted in HAG ("well-built, substantial")

name: Medora school
location_evidence: No location given.
notes: Earlier, a school opened at Little Missouri on Nov 5, 1883 (Dickinson Press, in HAG).

name: Peter Book's brickyard
location_evidence: No location given.
sources: NRHP 77001018 citing the Bad Lands Cow Boy (April 1884)
notes: Source of the yellow brick used in the church and the Von Hoffman House (inferred).

name: Clothing, drug and hardware stores; barber shop; saloons; brick houses
location_evidence: Not located. HAG says there were sometimes a dozen saloons or more.
sources: HAG (Medora chapter); Mandan Pioneer in HAG
notes: Use the BadlandsCowboy ad and notice data to name and date these.
